justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog & Search Container, Order & Checkout Container, Recommendation Container and Localization Container cover R-01, R-02, R-04. Reviews/ratings (R-03) only have a Review & Rating Aggregator, with no submission path or storage. Also inconsistent: the Recommendation Engine/ML Service is unconnected, and the shipping/tax flows are duplicated.
justifications.performance_efficiency: CloudFront SPA, OpenSearch, Session Cache (Redis), SQS asynchronous decoupling, Kinesis buffering and Debezium/MSK sync support the targets. Gaps: no catalog caching, no autoscaling or database read replicas, no explicit 3G optimization, and the SQLite local buffer limits scale.
justifications.compatibility: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping API and Tax Calculation Service are integrated via HTTPS/REST and SQS, and Localization Container handles currency. Inconsistencies remain: shipping is async at L1 but HTTPS/REST at L2, and no adapter or anti-corruption layer exists for the shipping APIs.
justifications.usability: The SPA serves buyers, admins and support through CloudFront, and Localization Context Provider and Compliance & Consent Banner help buyers. Support reps and admins have no dedicated functions or interfaces, Content Provider uses only API Gateway, and no accessibility or UX mechanisms are present.
justifications.reliability: Mechanisms exist: Route 53 latency routing, SQS decoupling, the Outbox Pattern, Debezium CDC and ElastiCache HA. But there is no multi-AZ/region failover, database replication, health checks, circuit breakers or backup/DR for 99.95%. The single API Gateway and the SQLite local buffer are weak points.
justifications.security: Strong: Cognito OAuth2/JWT, Auth & Token Validator, AWS WAF OWASP mitigations, rate limiting, mTLS via App Mesh, TLS 1.3, tokenized payments, encrypted PII, BOLA authorization, and PII Scrubber. Gaps: no audit logging, no key management, no explicit GDPR data-subject-rights handling.
justifications.maintainability: Clear decomposition into containers (Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Recommendation, Localization) with mesh-based routing and CDC decoupling. Weaknesses: the polyglot stack (Spring, Node, Python, Go), shared or ambiguous component definitions (Book Buyer as a component), a vague API Gateway, and no shared observability.
justifications.portability: Targets AWS with multi-region routing (Route 53, CloudFront). Containerized services and open technologies (PostgreSQL, Kafka, Envoy, OpenSearch) help. But heavy AWS lock-in (Cognito, SQS, Kinesis, App Mesh), and there is no IaC, container orchestration or data-residency per-region deployment definition.

sensitivity_points: No caching layer for catalog responses
Single PostgreSQL with no replicas shown
Autoscaling not specified
tradeoffs: mTLS gRPC hops add latency versus security
CDN speeds static assets, not dynamic API
PERF-01.justification: CloudFront, OpenSearch and throttling help, but no API caching, autoscaling or read replicas are shown. A 10x peak meeting 2 s on 3G is plausible but unproven.

sensitivity_points: Batch recompute is not separated from the online serving path
Shared data store for recommendation reads is unspecified
tradeoffs: Separate containers isolate compute but share unnamed storage
PERF-02.justification: Recommendations live in a separate container, which isolates CPU from catalog. But no offline batch pipeline, precomputed store or cache is described, and the ML service is vaguely external.

sensitivity_points: Inconsistent sync HTTPS versus async SQS shipping dispatch
Retry and DLQ policy unspecified
tradeoffs: Async shipping gives eventual consistency of shipment status
AVAIL-01.justification: SQS decoupling and the outbox pattern let checkout complete while shipping is deferred. The container diagram also shows a direct HTTPS call to shipping, and retry/DLQ details are missing.

sensitivity_points: No cross-region database replication described
Single PostgreSQL per service with no Multi-AZ stated
Failover health checks not defined
tradeoffs: Multi-region data replication costs versus GDPR data residency
AVAIL-02.justification: Route 53 and three regions are mentioned, but there is no data replication, multi-region deployment or failover design. Order loss on a us-east-1 failure is a real risk and 99.95% is not demonstrated.

sensitivity_points: Whether currencies are configuration-driven is unspecified
Payment gateway and tax currency support
Price storage model per currency
tradeoffs: Centralised localization eases change but couples checkout to it
MOD-01.justification: A dedicated Localization Container and currency engine localize the change. But there is no price or config model, and Order, SPA and payment adapters may all need edits. Feasible with some risk.

sensitivity_points: Stable gRPC contract at the API Gateway
Data Access Layer coupling to data schema
tradeoffs: Encapsulation gives easy swap but may limit data-model evolution
MOD-02.justification: Algorithm is isolated in the Personalization Engine behind a router and gRPC interface, so replacement stays in the container. A new algorithm needing different data or the external ML service could leak changes.

sensitivity_points: Review input sanitisation and output encoding in the SPA not described
Logging and alerting of blocked attacks not explicit
tradeoffs: WAF rules may cause false positives that hurt usability
SEC-01.justification: WAF, JSON schema validation, JPA parameterised access and OWASP mitigations are named at the edge. But XSS output encoding for reviews and explicit attack logging or monitoring are not shown.

sensitivity_points: No deletion orchestration across services
Verifiability and audit trail absent
PII in Order DB, Kinesis and logs
tradeoffs: Order retention obligations versus erasure requests
SEC-02.justification: PII scrubbing and a consent banner exist, but no deletion workflow, data inventory or audit mechanism spans the Order DB, caches, recommendations and the external email provider. Erasure would need significant new design.
